test_title: PYST 10: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 02 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In June 2025, the Government of India launched which of the following new disaster management tech platforms?

options.text: Integrated Centre Room for Emergency Response
Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response
Integrated Common Response for Emergency Response
Indian Control Room for Emergency Response

solution:
The correct answer is __**Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **June 2025** to enhance disaster management capabilities and provide a centralized platform for monitoring and responding to emergencies effectively.
 
• The ICR-ER is equipped with **state-of-the-art technology** such as advanced predictive analytics, GIS mapping, and real-time data integration to handle emergencies like **natural disasters, industrial accidents, and public health crises**.
 
• This platform aims to **coordinate disaster response efforts** across various government departments, ensuring rapid deployment of resources to affected areas.
 
• The ICR-ER also integrates data from multiple sources, including **satellite imagery, weather forecasting systems, and local disaster management authorities**, to provide comprehensive situational awareness.
 
• The initiative is a part of India's broader efforts to strengthen its disaster management infrastructure under frameworks like the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction** and India's **National Disaster Management Plan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the ICR-ER:**

 
 
• **Real-Time Surveillance:** The platform uses drones, CCTV, and satellite data to monitor disaster-hit areas.
 
• **Predictive Analytics:** Advanced AI tools predict potential disasters like floods or earthquakes based on historical data and environmental indicators.
 
• **GIS Mapping:** Geographical Information Systems are used to map affected areas and optimize resource allocation.
 
• **Mobile Connectivity:** The system ensures communication through mobile apps for citizens and disaster management teams.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005** provides the legal framework for disaster management in India.
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** is the apex body responsible for planning and coordinating disaster response.
 
• State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) and District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs) implement measures at local levels.
 
• India follows the **Sendai Framework (2015-2030)**, focusing on disaster risk reduction and building resilience.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Advanced Disaster Management Platforms:**
 
 
• **USA:** Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) uses centralized command centers for disaster response.
 
• **Japan:** Advanced earthquake early warning systems are integrated into disaster management platforms.
 
• **India:** The ICR-ER is a significant step toward leveraging technology for disaster preparedness and response.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The ICR-ER aligns with India's commitment to achieving the **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and Goal 13 (Climate Action).
 
• The platform is designed to be scalable and adaptable, allowing for integration with **future technologies** and evolving disaster scenarios.
 
• India has faced significant disasters, including floods, cyclones, and earthquakes, highlighting the need for robust disaster management systems.
 
• In addition to ICR-ER, India has other initiatives like the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (ITEWS)** and **DAMS Safety Programme** to mitigate specific risks.
